name: Power efficiency
answer: These measures show how much of the power a data center draws reaches the computing equipment, and how hard each rack is pushed. Dense GPU racks draw far more power than older server halls, so efficiency and density decide how much AI compute a site can run on the power it has.

metrics.line: The ratio of everything a facility draws from the grid to what its IT equipment alone consumes. A PUE of 1.5 means half again as much power goes to cooling, power conversion, and lighting as goes to the servers.
metrics.label: PUE, Power Usage Effectiveness

metrics.line: The same measurement as PUE expressed the other way round, IT energy as a percentage of total facility energy.
metrics.label: DCiE, Data Center Infrastructure Efficiency

metrics.line: Per-circuit measurement of how much of each breaker's rated capacity is in use, tracked continuously and at peak.
metrics.label: Breaker-level load and peak draw

metrics.line: The kilowatts delivered to and dissipated by a single rack. Traditional enterprise racks ran 5 to 15 kW; dense GPU training racks are specified at 40 to over 100 kW.
metrics.label: Power density per rack

reading.body:
Power efficiency in a data center is measured by how much of the grid draw reaches the IT equipment and how much power each rack can absorb. PUE and DCiE describe the same ratio from opposite directions, and breaker-level load tracking shows how close each circuit runs to its rated capacity.

The density figure is the one that changes the AI math. Traditional enterprise racks ran 5 to 15 kW, while dense GPU training racks are specified at 40 to over 100 kW. A facility built for the first cannot host the second without more power per rack and more cooling to match, so rack density and PUE together set the ceiling on how much compute a given grid connection supports.

What the data does not give is any actual PUE value, any site's measured load, or any comparison across operators or years. It defines the measures rather than reporting them. It also does not say where the power comes from or whether it arrives, which is the constraint that sits upstream of all of this.
